Softened the 15s health-check loop in monitor_relay_connections (src-tauri/src/lib.rs): removed the branches that pushed a Connected relay into unhealthy_relays for an empty/slow (>=2s) Metadata probe, a query error, or a timeout. Those cases now only call add_relay_log with the same diagnostic messages (kept for visibility); update_relay_metrics(ping_ms/last_check) is still recorded for any completed round-trip including empty/slow ones (Ok(Ok(events)) branch), but not for errors/timeouts since there's no round-trip time to record. Extracted the force-reconnect condition into a pure fn relay_needs_forced_reconnect(status) -> bool (Terminated | Disconnected) used in the else-if branch, with 2 unit tests (relay_health_reconnect_tests, both passing). The Terminated/Disconnected branch that feeds unhealthy_relays -> disconnect()+try_connect() is kept intact and unchanged in behavior — this is required because the separate 5s terminated-poller at the bottom of the same function only checks status == RelayStatus::Terminated, not Disconnected, so this 15s loop remains the only automatic-recovery path for Disconnected relays; added a one-line comment above the health-check task noting this split of responsibility. Did not touch the StatusChanged listener task, the 5s terminated-poller, fetch_messages, SyncMode, ChatState, or deep_rescan. Verified with cargo check --lib (clean, only pre-existing unrelated warnings) and cargo test --lib relay_health_reconnect_tests (2 passed).

Added SyncMode::CatchUp + ChatState.last_catch_up_until (u64, init 0). fetch_messages(false) no longer dead-ends at Finished: extracted pure helpers catch_up_window(window_start, now, apply_overlap) and should_promote_to_catch_up(mode, is_syncing, last_catch_up_until, now) (grace=60s, overlap=30s, slice=2days). When Finished and stale (grace elapsed) and not already syncing, promotes to CatchUp and walks FORWARD in <=2-day slices from last_catch_up_until to now, emitting sync_slice_finished between slices and sync_finished + last_catch_up_until=now on the slice that reaches now (mirrors existing ForwardSync/BackwardSync/DeepRescan slice-chaining via frontend's sync_slice_finished listener). Within grace window: still returns immediately via existing Finished early-return, no network call. is_syncing guard (already true whenever mode!=Finished, plus explicit !is_syncing check in should_promote_to_catch_up) prevents a second trigger from re-promoting/spawning a parallel window while one is in flight. last_catch_up_until is advanced only in the shared should_continue=false completion block (BackwardSync/DeepRescan exhausting empty iterations, or CatchUp reaching now) -- there's no distinguishable failed-vs-empty signal today (relay stream errors panic via .unwrap() before reaching this point), documented inline. DeepRescan/ForwardSync/BackwardSync semantics, monitor_relay_connections, and deep_rescan untouched. Added mod catch_up_tests with 7 unit tests covering: grace boundary, AE1 (1hr-stale -> single 2-day window ending at now), wide-gap forward multi-slice walk with termination at now, and the is_syncing in-flight guard blocking promotion. cargo check -p pacto and cargo test -p pacto --lib catch_up_tests both pass cleanly (only pre-existing unrelated warnings).

Corrected the plan's inaccurate R12 problem framing before implementing: the plan claimed fetch_messages(handle, false, Some(url)) is a no-op because it 'returns immediately since sync_mode == Finished'. That is false — src-tauri/src/lib.rs's fetch_messages, in the 'if relay_url.is_some()' branch (originally lines 752-780, now ~789-819), runs unconditionally BEFORE any state.sync_mode check exists in the function; the Finished early-return only applies to the relay_url.is_none() path. The single-relay fetch already executed and processed real events on every Connected transition. The actual historical bug (per docs/solutions/logic-errors/orphaned-relay-health-monitor-command.md) was monitor_relay_connections() never being invoked from the frontend, already fixed separately via runPostLoginNetworkSync.

Given that, fixed the two things genuinely wrong with the single-relay path instead:
1. Unconditional fixed 2-day window on every Connected event, ignoring any recent account-wide catch-up. Added pure helper single_relay_fetch_since(last_catch_up_until, now) = max(now - CATCH_UP_SLICE_SECS, last_catch_up_until.saturating_sub(CATCH_UP_OVERLAP_SECS)), reusing U1's CATCH_UP_SLICE_SECS/CATCH_UP_OVERLAP_SECS constants. Wired into fetch_messages' relay_url branch via a read-only STATE.lock().await.last_catch_up_until (no ChatState mutation). 3 unit tests cover: no-prior-catch-up falls back to full 2-day cap, recent catch-up narrows the window, long outage stays capped at 2 days (all in catch_up_tests mod).
2. No overlap guard: rapid Connected/Disconnected/Connected flapping could spawn multiple concurrent single-relay fetches for the same relay. Added RELAY_FETCH_IN_FLIGHT (lazy_static Mutex<HashSet<String>>, same pattern as WRAPPER_ID_CACHE) plus pure relay_fetch_may_start(in_flight, url) helper. The Connected branch now inserts into the set before spawning and removes on completion; different relays get independent slots. 3 unit tests in relay_health_reconnect_tests mod cover same-relay blocking, different-relay independence, and slot release.

Did not touch fetch_messages' relay_url.is_none() path, the 15s health loop/relay_needs_forced_reconnect, deep_rescan, or account-wide ChatState fields beyond the read-only lock. Verified: cargo check --lib clean; cargo test --lib -- catch_up_tests relay_health_reconnect_tests: 15/15 passed.
